## Why

An agent evaluation can start from a real conversation at a chosen turn. It needs two things: the conversation before that turn, and the trip as it stood when the user sent that turn's message. The coordinator then runs the turn on today's code, and the evaluation scores what it said and saved. Example: the Bar Harbor session's turn 5, where the coordinator raised `comfortableDrivingInHours` to cover one long day (#167).

The transcript already keeps the conversation (persistence design, section 6). Nothing keeps the trip. The database holds each trip only as it is now, after every later turn. So a past turn can't be set up again.

This issue saves a copy of the trip at the start of every turn, so every session from now on can be a starting point for evaluations. A later issue rebuilds these copies for the Bar Harbor session, which ran before they existed, and another starts a run from any turn.

A **trip version** is a copy of everything the coordinator reads about a trip, as it stood when one turn started: the plan (the trip brief and the itinerary, persistence design section 2), the trip's places, trip memory, and the user's memory.

It's also most of what #147 would need, if that idea goes ahead. #147's open questions note that the itinerary keeps no history today.

## Design

- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), sections 2 (what is stored together), 6 (sessions and transcripts, and deleting a trip), 8.5 (sessions), and 8.8 (memory).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.5 (memory visibility, which covers forgetting an item).

## Decided

- **A version is saved when a turn starts, before the coordinator runs.** Not at the end of the turn before. The start includes changes made between turns, such as another session's edits, or a memory item the user forgot in the chat view's memory list. An evaluation needs the trip as the coordinator found it.
- **Each version is whole, not a list of changes.** A session has tens of turns, so the size is fine, and restoring one is a single copy.
- **Each version is tied to its turn's place in the transcript,** so a run can cut the transcript right before that turn's user message. The implementer picks how, such as the turn's number in the session, counted the way `src/agent/shown-messages.ts` counts user messages.
- **The app never reads versions.** Only evaluation tooling does. The coordinator never sees them.
- **Deleting a trip deletes its versions,** in the same transaction as the rest of the trip (persistence design, section 6).
- **A forgotten memory item stays in older versions.** "Forgotten items no longer influence recommendations" (functional spec 10.5) still holds, since the app never reads versions. The transcript already keeps the user's words, so versions keep nothing that wasn't kept already.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add a table for trip versions, with a migration: one row per turn, keyed to its session and its turn.
- Save a version at the start of every coordinator turn, in `CoordinatorTurns` (`src/agent/coordinator-turns.ts`), which both the app's API and `npm run chat` use. Save it after the checks that can refuse the turn, such as a closed chat or a turn already running, so a refused message saves nothing.
- Remove a trip's versions in `TripWriter.deleteTrip()`.
- Write trip versions into the persistence design: what a version holds, when it's saved, and that a trip's delete removes them.
- Add tests with fake repositories (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A session with three turns on the local stack (systems design, section 6) has three versions. Each matches the trip as it stood when its turn started. Check it by hand by forgetting a memory item between turns 2 and 3: the item is in version 2 and not in version 3.
- Deleting the trip removes its versions.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
